changes.old: Amends Ala. Code Sections 40-9B-3, 40-9B-4, 40-9B-4.1, and 40-23-35. Limits data processing center abatement periods beginning 2027-01-01, generally to 20 years, with added 10-year extension paths for certain investments. Requires certain 100 MW-plus data processing centers to pay state noneducational ad valorem taxes and sales/use tax on specified construction, power, backup generation, and battery purchases beginning 2027-01-01, subject to targeted-county gubernatorial authority. Extends the data processing center abatement sunset.
changes.new: Amends Alabama data-processing-center tax abatements and sales-tax distribution. For qualifying abatements granted on or after January 1, 2027, revised duration tiers generally permit up to 20 years, with a conditional additional 10 years for qualified local investments. For centers with at least 100 MW peak demand, specified state noneducational ad valorem and construction-related transaction tax abatements generally end when property is placed in service, subject to eligible equipment and targeted-county gubernatorial exceptions. Extends the incentive application sunset and excludes specified incentives in projects executed before the effective date and expansions of those projects during the following ten years from the amendments to Sections 40-9B-3, 40-9B-4 and 40-9B-4.1. Act effective June 1, 2026.

changes.old: Adds Ala. Code Section 37-4-22.1. Defines a "large load data center customer" as a data processing center customer with expected total peak demand of 150 MW or greater on contiguous parcels. Directs PSC public-interest review of retail electric service contracts to consider recovery of incremental costs from the data center and positive benefits for other retail electric customers.
changes.new: Adds Ala. Code Section 37-4-22.1. Defines a large load data center customer as a contracted retail customer with expected peak demand of at least 150 MW on contiguous parcels, meeting the statutory data processing center definition and operating solely for data processing. PSC public-interest review considers recovery of incremental costs and positive benefits to other retail customers.

changes.old: Not a moratorium. Directly regulates data centers and utility service. The committee substitute requires data centers to pay facility-driven utility costs, provide financial security for utility capital investments above $1 million, use contracts that avoid fuel-supply and reliability risk shifting, include backup power and reliability planning, execute municipal CBAs, address waste heat, water use, broadband interconnection, digital equity, and file decommissioning and recycling plans. The committee substitute exempts data centers below 15 MW peak electric demand and 1.5 billion standard cubic feet of annual gas use.
changes.new: Not a moratorium. Directly regulates data centers and utility service. The committee substitute requires data centers to pay facility-driven utility costs, provide financial security for utility capital investments above $1 million, use contracts that avoid fuel-supply and reliability risk shifting, include backup power and reliability planning, execute municipal CBAs, address waste heat, water use, broadband interconnection, digital equity, and file decommissioning and recycling plans. The committee substitute exempts data centers consuming both less than 15 MW peak electric demand and less than 1.5 billion standard cubic feet of gas annually.
